precepts.text: The galleries of the temple round about on their three stories.
precepts.point: The heavens are built in stories, like the three stories of the temple and the ark.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Solomon built the temple as a resemblance of the holy tabernacle in heaven, so the temple's layout tells us about the heavens. Ezekiel 41:16: “The door posts, and the narrow windows, and the galleries round about on their three stories”. Three stories, three floors. Read on and it tells you there are chambers, a chamber here and a chamber there, the way 2 Esdras speaks of the chambers of souls.

It is no coincidence that the temple was built with three stories. It goes into the same thing Paul mentioned: the third heaven, where paradise is. The levels of the temple match the levels of the heavens: the sky of this earth, then space, then paradise. And above them all is the Father, at the very top, like the holy of holies.

So the three stories of Ezekiel's temple help explain “caught up to the third heaven.” Paul was taken up to the top story God built, paradise, which was made in the beginning when God made the firmament and called it heaven.

points: The angel brings Ezekiel to the temple itself and measures the posts six cubits broad on each side, about nine feet, the breadth of the tabernacle. The door is ten cubits and its sides five cubits on each side.

note.label: Ezekiel 41: The Measure of the Temple and the Most Holy Place

points: He measures the length forty cubits and the breadth twenty, then goes inward and measures twenty cubits by twenty before the temple, and tells Ezekiel this is the most holy place.

note.label: Ezekiel 41: The Measure of the Temple and the Most Holy Place

points: The wall of the house is six cubits, and the side chambers four cubits round about, three chambers one over another and thirty in order. The chambers rest on the wall but have no hold in the wall of the house itself. There are ninety side rooms, likely used for storing.

note.label: Ezekiel 41: The Measure of the Temple and the Most Holy Place

points: There is a winding stair going up round about the house, so the breadth of the house increases upward from the lowest chamber to the highest. The doors of the side chambers face the open place, one toward the north and another toward the south.

note.label: Ezekiel 41: The Measure of the Temple and the Most Holy Place

points: The building before the separate place toward the west is seventy cubits broad, its wall five cubits thick, and its length ninety cubits. He measures the house a hundred cubits long, and the separate place and building with their walls a hundred cubits.

note.label: Ezekiel 41: The Measure of the Temple and the Most Holy Place

points: The breadth of the face of the house and the separate place toward the east is a hundred cubits, and the building over against the separate place with its galleries on each side is also a hundred cubits.

note.label: Ezekiel 41: The Measure of the Temple and the Most Holy Place

points: The inner temple, the porches, the doorposts, the windows, and the galleries on three stories are sealed with wood round about from the ground up to the windows. The walls are made with cherubim and palm trees, a palm tree between every two cherubim.

note.label: Ezekiel 41: The Measure of the Temple and the Most Holy Place

points: Every cherub has two faces, the face of a man toward the palm tree on one side and the face of a young lion toward the palm tree on the other, made through all the house from the ground to above the door. The altar of wood is three cubits high, and the angel says this is the table that is before the Lord.

note.label: Ezekiel 41: The Measure of the Temple and the Most Holy Place

points: The sanctuary and the temple each have two doors with two turning leaves apiece, carved with cherubim and palm trees like those on the walls. There are thick planks upon the face of the porch, and narrow windows and palm trees on the sides.

note.label: Ezekiel 41: The Measure of the Temple and the Most Holy Place
